what_happened: At an intersection with a RIGHT command, the ego crept forward at about 2 m/s. It drifted left of its planned right-turn path, ending about 3.2 m off the recorded trajectory. It drove into the path of actor 112, which was turning left across the intersection toward the ego's side. The ego slowed only slightly (2.4 to 1.7 m/s) as the gap closed from 26 m to 4.6 m, and hit 112 with its front.

The command was RIGHT and the recorded path curved right toward the turn. Instead, the ego kept drifting left across lanes at about 9–10 m/s, then ran over the left lane edge onto the grass median near the intersection at 9.0 s, about 6.2 m from the recorded path. The camera view was clean before the failure, so the policy's steering caused this.

The route said turn right, but the ego crept into the intersection at about 2.6 m/s and steered left of its route, ending about 4 m off the recorded path. Oncoming car 112 was turning left across the intersection in plain view, and the ego hit it head-on with its front without yielding or braking in time.

On the RIGHT command, the ego turned right at the intersection much more sharply than the recorded human path. It cut toward the curb and drove front-first into parked car 90 at about 4 m/s, ending 7 m off the recorded path.

On a RIGHT command at an urban intersection, the ego crept through the turn at about 3 m/s. Its planned path (orange) hooked toward the curb lane of parked cars, and it drove its front into parked car 90 (dark sedan, close on the left of the camera at 9.6s), ending 5.3 m off the human trajectory and partly off the drivable area.

The command was RIGHT and the route bent right toward the intersection, but the policy kept planning a path that veered left. The ego drifted left out of its lane at about 9–10 m/s and ran onto the planted median with palm trees, ending 6.1 m from the recorded trajectory. The camera view was clean before the drift, so a rendering problem does not explain the mistake.

The route command was RIGHT, but the ego stayed in the leftmost lane at about 10 m/s while the recorded path moved right. Its plan then curved left, and the ego drove onto the landscaped median with palm trees at 8.9 s, about 6 m off the recorded trajectory.

With a RIGHT command at the intersection, the ego turned right far too tightly and early instead of following the recorded path, which kept going farther through the intersection before turning. The camera view was clean before the turn and only smeared at impact.

The ego was told to turn RIGHT at the intersection. The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path moved right, but the ego's plan kept bending left out of its lane. No other actor was involved, and the camera view was clean until the ego was already on the median.

The ego was finishing a right turn at about 4 m/s into a narrow street lined with parked cars. Instead of following the recorded path toward the middle or right of the street, it kept to the left and its front hit parked car 68 at the corner of the street entrance, about 1.5 m off the recorded path.

After the policy took over at 4.7 s, the ego kept going at about 9.5 m/s and its planned path bent left, away from the recorded path (about 1.2 m off by the end). Its front-left corner hit actor 33, which was moving alongside in the left lane, at 6.4 s, while the lead vehicle was still about 17 m ahead.

One second after the policy took over, the ego was flagged offroad at the stop line of a large intersection at about 8.9 m/s. The route turns right here, but the policy's plan went straight and then veered left, and the command showed STRAIGHT until the failure frame. Even so, the ego was only 0.5 m from the human's recorded path when flagged, so the offroad call may come from the map edge at the intersection entrance rather than a real departure.

Despite a RIGHT command, the ego steered left across the yellow centre line. It drove at about 11.5 m/s in the oncoming lane, about 10 m off the recorded path, and hit oncoming van 86 head-on without braking.

While turning right at the intersection at about 4 m/s, the ego cut the corner far tighter than the recorded human path (6.9 m off it at failure). Its front hit car 90, which was parked along the curb of the street it was turning into.

Parked car 68 sat in that path, and the ego never braked as the gap closed from 10 m to 4 m, so its front hit the parked car. The rear contact came only after this.

This was a lateral drift into a parked roadside car, not a lead vehicle in its lane, a turn, or leaving the road; the rear contact came later.

The policy's planned path points straight or slightly left, even though the command had just switched to RIGHT, so this looks more like a small edge-of-lane or map-boundary clip than a clear steering mistake.

Although the route command was RIGHT, the ego drifted left across the double yellow centre line into the oncoming lanes and kept going at about 11 m/s.
